speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are presenting with wrist pain, fever, and skin lesions; can you tell me exactly how long you have had these symptoms and if they appeared at the same time?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The timeline of your wrist pain following a knee issue and a camping trip is concerning. Can you describe the appearance and location of these skin lesions?

REQUEST IMAGES: Dermatology_lesions

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Lyme Arthritis (Borrelia burgdorferi infection). The combination of recent Minnesota camping, a self-resolving monoarticular knee infection, and now a septic wrist with violaceous vesiculopustular lesions is classic for Lyme disease.
